description: Kashmiri Pink Tea, also known as Noon Chai, is a traditional Pakistani and Kashmiri beverage known for its distinctive pink hue and rich, creamy texture. This savory-sweet tea is brewed with special tea leaves, baking soda, and milk, creating a comforting and unique flavor profile. It is often garnished with crushed pistachios or almonds, making it a delightful treat for any time of day.

instructions.title: Prepare the Qahwa (Tea Concentrate)
instructions.text: In a large saucepan, combine Kashmiri tea leaves, baking soda, and 3 cups of cold water. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low and let it simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally. The liquid should reduce and turn a deep reddish-brown color, which is crucial for the pink color development.

instructions.title: Aerate the Qahwa
instructions.text: Remove the saucepan from the heat. Vigorously 'aerate' the tea concentrate by pouring it from a height into another pot and back again. Repeat this process for 5-7 minutes. This traditional 'phetna' technique helps to incorporate air, cool the tea, and develop the beautiful pink hue. Alternatively, use a ladle to repeatedly lift and drop the tea from a height.

instructions.title: Add Ice Cold Water
instructions.text: After aeration, add 1 cup of ice cold water (or a few ice cubes) to the tea concentrate. Return the saucepan to the stove and bring it back to a boil. Let it simmer for another 5-10 minutes. The thermal shock from the cold water further helps to deepen and set the pink color.

instructions.title: Strain the Concentrate
instructions.text: Carefully strain the prepared tea concentrate (qahwa) through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean, separate pot. Discard the used tea leaves. You should now have a concentrated, deep maroon-colored liquid that is the base for your pink tea.

instructions.title: Combine with Milk and Spices
instructions.text: To the strained qahwa, add the full-fat milk, salt, and lightly crushed green cardamom pods. If you prefer a sweet tea, add sugar at this stage. Stir well to combine all ingredients.

instructions.title: Simmer to Perfection
instructions.text: Place the pot with the tea and milk mixture back on medium-low heat. Bring it to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to low and let it simmer for another 5-10 minutes, stirring occasionally. This simmering allows the flavors to meld and the tea to reach its desired creaminess and temperature. The tea should now have transformed into a beautiful, appealing pink color.

instructions.title: Serve Hot and Garnish
instructions.text: Once the Kashmiri Pink Tea is perfectly pink and hot, pour it into individual serving cups. Garnish generously with crushed pistachios and optional sliced almonds before serving. Enjoy this comforting and unique Pakistani beverage immediately.

tips: The vigorous aeration (phetna) of the tea concentrate is critical for achieving the vibrant pink color. Do not skip this step, as it is the secret to authentic Kashmiri Pink Tea.
Always use full-fat milk for the creamiest and most authentic Kashmiri Pink Tea. Skim milk or low-fat milk will not provide the same rich texture and mouthfeel.
Adjust the amount of salt and sugar according to your personal preference. Some prefer it purely savory, while others enjoy a slightly sweet balance. Taste and adjust before the final simmer.
article:
**Kashmiri Pink Tea: A Sip of Tradition and Elegance**

In the vibrant tapestry of Pakistani beverages, few stand out with the unique charm and visual appeal of Kashmiri Pink Tea. More than just a drink, this beautiful rose-hued concoction is a warm embrace of culture, a testament to generations of culinary tradition, and an absolute delight for the senses. Often referred to as Noon Chai, this salted tea from the valleys of Kashmir has found a beloved place in homes and cafes across Pakistan, especially during the colder months or for special occasions. Its distinctive preparation process, coupled with a delicate balance of flavors, makes it an unforgettable experience. Join us to uncover the magic behind Kashmiri Pink Tea.

## What is Kashmiri Pink Tea?

Kashmiri Pink Tea, also known as Noon Chai, is a traditional salted tea originating from the picturesque Kashmir Valley. Unlike conventional teas, this beverage boasts a striking salmon-pink to reddish-brown color, a hue achieved through a fascinating chemical reaction during its preparation. The base is a special green tea leaf, often called "Kashmiri chai patti," which is boiled vigorously with a pinch of baking soda. This alkaline environment, combined with continuous aeration (known as "phainna"), oxidizes the tea's chlorophyll, releasing the characteristic pink pigment.

Traditionally, Kashmiri Pink Tea is a savory beverage, seasoned with salt. However, its popularity across Pakistan has led to variations where it's sweetened and adorned with crushed nuts like almonds and pistachios, sometimes with a touch of cardamom. The result is a creamy, comforting, and subtly spiced drink
